clue.text: American setter's parting words: 'Shoot slightly upwind'

parts.note: a setter leaving would say I'M OFF, the setter speaking of themself

explanation.surface: An American crossword setter signs off with some shooting advice.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted phrase looks like the setter's farewell, but the farewell is only the wordplay; the quotation is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To aim off is a marksman's term for pointing a little to one side to allow for wind.

clue.text: A variety of claret that's very hard to confuse with Poitiers'

indicators.note: to confuse letters is to jumble them, so this calls for a rearrangement

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wine buff warns that one claret is easily mistaken for a Poitiers vintage.
explanation.walkthrough: Claret is not wine here but old slang for blood, so a variety of it is a blood group. 'to confuse' scrambles V, H and POITIERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhesus positive is a blood group, and claret is British slang for blood.

clue.text: Semi-aquatic mammal picked up north of Washington capital

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits above, or north of, the second
something picked up is heard, so a word that sounds like the mammal is used

parts.note: the otter lives both on land and in water
WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington State

explanation.surface: An otter is spotted somewhere up north of Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: OTTA is said like OTTER in a non-rhotic accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is the capital city of Canada, which lies north of Washington State.

clue.text: Compound rate's void in Ukraine

indicators.note: the emptied word goes inside the abbreviation for Ukraine

parts.note: UA is the international code for Ukraine

indicators.note: a void word is emptied of its inside, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A financial report says some exchange rate means nothing in Ukraine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound' looks like a verb or an adjective, but it is the chemistry noun; 'void' leaves only the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Urea is a nitrogen compound found in urine and used in fertilisers.

clue.text: November or May touring North Dakota's French region

parts.note: N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the month wraps around the state abbreviation

parts.note: taken as written
ND is the postal abbreviation for North Dakota

explanation.surface: A traveller plans to tour North Dakota in November or May.
explanation.definitionFit: Normandy is a region of northern France, famous for the 1944 landings.

clue.text: Put on clothing for international singer from Canada

indicators.note: clothing a thing is wrapping it, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: to don clothes is to put them on

explanation.surface: A Canadian singer dresses up for an international show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' puts DON around I.
explanation.definitionFit: Celine Dion is the Quebec-born singer famous for My Heart Will Go On.

clue.text: Kim leaves Himalayan state hospital a religious adherent

indicators.note: when a person leaves, they are taken away, so these letters are removed

parts.note: Sikkim is a small Indian state in the Himalayas
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A woman called Kim leaves a Himalayan hospital, met by a believer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' removes KIM from SIKKIM, leaving SIK.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sikh follows Sikhism, the faith founded by Guru Nanak in the Punjab.

clue.text: Trunk road primarily going on to Somalia

indicators.note: going on means following on after, so the road's first letter comes after the word to
primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of road is used

parts.note: SO is the international code for Somalia

explanation.surface: A trunk road heads mainly towards Somalia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk road' reads as one phrase, but 'Trunk' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human body, without the head and limbs.

clue.text: Batik: the first cut, woven fabric of Asia

indicators.note: woven letters are worked into a new pattern, so they are rearranged
with the first cut, the opening letter of the word is cut off

explanation.surface: Batik's first cut is woven into an Asian fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first cut' drops B from BATIK, and 'woven' shuffles ATIK.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikat is a South-East Asian cloth whose threads are dyed in patterns before weaving.

clue.text: Nemesis roller coaster ride for Faroes shortly to welcome children

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside the other
a roller coaster throws its riders about, so the letters are thrown into a new order
shortly means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: the Faroes, or Faroe Islands, lie in the North Atlantic

explanation.surface: A dreaded roller coaster ride in the Faroes awaits the children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' drops the final S, 'roller coaster ride for' scrambles what is left into ARFOE, and 'to welcome' takes the children's abbreviation inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch-foe is a chief enemy, the sense of a personal nemesis.

clue.text: Oriental setting for 'edgy work' from Beatles wife and naked mystic?

parts.note: Yoko Ono married John Lennon of the Beatles

indicators.note: naked means stripped, so the word loses its outer letters

parts.note: a shaman is a mystic healer who contacts the spirit world

explanation.surface: A Beatle's wife and an unclothed mystic stage provocative art in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naked' strips SHAMAN to HAMA. The quoted 'edgy work' seems to nod to Yoko Ono's avant-garde art, and plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Yokohama is a large Japanese port city, the Orient being an old term for East Asia.

clue.text: India's boxing champ? Just the opposite in Olympic venue

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so one piece goes around the other
this reverses the boxing, so the chewing word encloses the letter for India

parts.note: to champ is to munch noisily
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: India's boxing champion competes at the Olympics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'champ' looks like a boxer but is a verb meaning chew. 'boxing' says I goes around MUNCH, and 'Just the opposite' flips it so MUNCH goes around I.
explanation.definitionFit: Munich in Germany hosted the 1972 Summer Olympic Games.

clue.text: One day California will supply an entire continent

parts.note: A means one, as in a single thing
FRI is the short form of Friday
CA is the postal abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: A prophecy that one day California will feed a whole continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One day' reads as 'some day', but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Africa is the second-largest of the world's continents.

clue.text: Acclaimed singer provided by Spain for their holiday spot

indicators.note: acclaimed is read as called out loud, so the word for the singer is said rather than spelt

parts.note: a tenor is a male singer with a high voice
provided means if, as in on condition that
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Spain lays on a celebrated singer at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acclaimed' looks like praise, but it means cried aloud, so TENOR is spelt TENER.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenerife, the largest Canary Island, is a popular resort for sun-seeking tourists.

clue.text: Hebridean island in which I will occupy log home?

indicators.note: to occupy a place is to sit inside it, so the letter goes within

parts.note: a log comes from a tree, its original home

explanation.surface: Someone muses about living in a log cabin on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'log home' sounds like a log cabin, but it is where a log came from.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiree is a flat, windy island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.

clue.text: April wind swirling round a city in Pakistan

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the single letter
swirling letters are whirled about, so they come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A spring wind blows around a Pakistani city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirling' scrambles APRILWIND, and 'round' wraps it around A.
explanation.definitionFit: Rawalpindi is a major city in the Punjab, home to the Pakistan Army headquarters.

clue.text: Capital city determining itself leaves Indonesia for starters

indicators.note: starters are the opening letters, so each word gives its first letter

explanation.surface: A capital decides for itself to leave Indonesia.
explanation.walkthrough: Dili really did leave Indonesia: East Timor gained independence in 2002.
explanation.definitionFit: Dili is the capital of East Timor, formerly occupied by Indonesia.

clue.text: Italy's sparkling water maintaining its river crustaceans' order

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so the water holds the river inside

parts.note: soda is fizzy water
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: Italian fizzy water from one of the country's rivers contains crustaceans.
explanation.definitionFit: Isopoda is the order of crustaceans that includes woodlice and their water-dwelling relatives.

clue.text: Revolutionary communist near to getting authority in the Midlands

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a Red is a communist
by means near to, as in standing by the door

explanation.surface: A revolutionary communist edges towards power in the English Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary communist' looks like one political phrase, but 'Revolutionary' turns RED round.
explanation.definitionFit: Derby is a city in the East Midlands with its own unitary council.

clue.text: Sail away after Germany, one nation in 13

indicators.note: the sail and away come after the letter for Germany

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
a jib is a triangular sail
out means away, as in out of the office
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone sets sail after leaving Germany for an African country.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is AFRICA, the answer at 13-across.
explanation.definitionFit: Djibouti is a small country in the Horn of Africa, on the Gulf of Aden.

clue.text: Expression of relief as man found in outskirts of Warsaw

indicators.note: the male pronoun is found inside the edge letters
the outskirts are the edges, so only the first and last letters are used

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: Relief as a missing man turns up on the edge of Warsaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Whew is a sigh or exclamation of relief, a variant of phew.

clue.text: Three times oyster content gets sent back in US national park

indicators.note: something sent back goes the other way, so the letters are read backwards
the content is what lies inside, so the letters are drawn from within these words

explanation.surface: A diner returns a dish of oysters three times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' finds ETIMESOY inside 'Three times oyster', and 'gets sent back' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Yosemite in California is a celebrated US national park known for granite cliffs and waterfalls.

clue.text: Seaport of Bali unfortunately overwhelmed by bad smell

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are swamped by the smell, which surrounds them

parts.note: BO is body odour

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A seaside town in Bali is overpowered by a stink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seaport of Bali' looks like one phrase, but the port is in Spain. 'unfortunately' scrambles the island to ILBA, and 'overwhelmed by' wraps the smell around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilbao is a Basque port city in northern Spain.

clue.text: Superhero gets New York to replace trademark tree

indicators.note: one pair of letters takes the place of the other

parts.note: Batman is the DC Comics superhero

explanation.surface: A superhero arrives in New York to replace a brand.
explanation.definitionFit: The banyan is an Indian fig whose aerial roots grow down into new trunks.

clue.text: Complex system in Saudi regularly defied understanding

indicators.note: the network word goes inside the picked letters
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: a maze is a complex network of paths

explanation.surface: A complicated set-up in Saudi Arabia baffled everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes A and D from SAUDI.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that amazed people astonished them, being beyond what they could grasp.

clue.text: Informed Ohio about drug manufacturing centre there

indicators.note: about means around, so the first pieces go around the drug

parts.note: told means informed
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone tells Ohio about a drug-making operation in the state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there' points back to Ohio.
explanation.definitionFit: Toledo, Ohio is an industrial city known for glass and car production.

clue.text: Hebridean island in which I will occupy starter home?

indicators.note: to occupy a place is to sit inside it, so the letter goes within

parts.note: an egg is where a creature's life starts, so it is its first home

explanation.walkthrough: A starter home is a first house for buyers, but here it is the egg a chick starts life in.

clue.text: Brazil almost beaten by largely unconventional island group of 13

indicators.note: by means beside, so the two pieces sit next to each other
largely means for the most part, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: zany means wacky or unconventional

indicators.note: beaten letters are knocked about into a new order
almost means not quite, so the last letter goes

parts.note: taken as written, as the country

explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims BRAZIL to BRAZI, which 'beaten' scrambles to ZIBAR; 'largely' cuts ZANY to ZAN. 13 is AFRICA.

clue.text: Area of Zambia concerned with energy

parts.note: Z is the international vehicle code for Zambia
on means about or concerned with, as in a talk on art
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A part of Zambia focused on power supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: A zone is a region or area set apart for some purpose.

clue.text: Spend some time relaxing in Shanghai

indicators.note: in means inside, so the letters are found within the city name

explanation.surface: A tourist chills out for a while in Shanghai.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang, or hang out, is informal for idling away time in a relaxed way.

clue.text: Thailand women leaving money for Pacific kingdom

parts.note: T is the international vehicle code for Thailand

indicators.note: the letter for women leaves, so it is removed

parts.note: wonga is British slang for cash

explanation.surface: Women leave Thailand with their money for a South Seas kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: Wonga is everyday British slang for money; without W it gives ONGA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is a Polynesian island nation ruled by a king.

clue.text: Expecting Lima to fight

parts.note: a pregnant woman who is due is expecting a baby
L is Lima in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A traveller expects a fight in Lima.

explanation.definitionFit: A duel is a formal fight between two people, as with pistols at dawn.
